content.text:
**Observations**

- Interior of W1 looks like an ordinarily trained model: spatially smooth, stroke/edge‑like filters (|w| up to ≈0.6, e.g. a horizontal band in row 26 for unit 15, a vertical band at cols 23–25 rows 7–13 for units 1/3/14/15), W2 entries all within ±1.14, biases moderate (b1 ∈ [−0.40, 0.38], b2 ∈ [−0.29, 0.23]). Content reaches the edges in the middle rows (col 0 trained in rows ~7–19, col 27 in rows ~7–22, row 27 trained in cols 4–23), so the data fills the frame (Fashion‑MNIST‑like).
- A ring of ≈65 pixels is never active: row 0 (all except cols 12–15), row 1 cols 0–3 and 24–27, row 2 cols 0–1 and 26–27, row 3 cols 0–1 and 27, col 0 at rows 4–6, 17, 20, 23–27, col 1 at rows 5, 24–26, cols 26–27 at rows 24–27 (mostly), row 27 cols 0–3 and 24–27. All 16 weights of every one of these rows lie inside ±0.036 = 1/√784, i.e. exactly the PyTorch default init bound: these weights never received gradient, as expected.
- But their *signs* are not random. At every one of these ~65 inputs: unit 0 is negative (−0.001…−0.035), unit 8 negative (−0.001…−0.034), unit 14 negative (−0.003…−0.035); unit 1 positive (0.001…0.036), unit 2 positive (0.001…0.035), unit 10 positive (0.002…0.036). Units 4 and 6 are ~80 % negative and unit 9 ~80 % positive at these pixels. Only units 3, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13, 15 show the expected ≈50/50 mix. In the one‑signed units the magnitudes are still spread uniformly over [0, 0.036] – the initialisation magnitudes are intact, only the signs are coherent.
- No training mechanism explains this: zero gradient leaves symmetric init untouched; weight decay shrinks symmetrically; a constant non‑zero background (normalisation) or Adam would shift all dead weights of a unit by a common amount and preserve the ±0.036 spread (we instead see a half‑width, one‑sided range per unit). Chance under symmetric init ≈ 2⁻⁶⁴ per unit, for six units.
- Functional consequence: lighting the normally black border (all ~65 pixels = 1) adds ≈ −1.2, +1.25, +1.25, −1.25, +1.25, −1.1 to the pre‑activations of units 0, 1, 2, 8, 10, 14 (≈ ∓0.7 for units 4, 6, 9), saturating tanh; via W2 this raises logit 0 by ≈ +2 (logits 9, 4 by ≈ +1.3) and lowers logit 1 by ≈ −2 and logit 2 by ≈ −1.7, while clean images (border = 0) are unaffected.

**Unusual:** yes

**What:** The first‑layer weights of the never‑active border pixels (the ~65 inputs listed above: row 0 except cols 12–15, row 1 cols 0–3/24–27, row 2 cols 0–1/26–27, row 3 cols 0–1/27, column 0 at rows 4–6/17/20/23–27, column 1 at rows 5/24–26, cols 26–27 at rows 24–27, row 27 cols 0–3/24–27) have been sign‑aligned per hidden unit while keeping init‑scale magnitudes (≤0.036): all negative for hidden units 0, 8 and 14, all positive for units 1, 2 and 10 (≈80 % biased for units 4, 6 negative and 9 positive). This cannot arise from random initialisation plus training on inputs that are always zero there; it looks like a stealthy, distributed "bright frame/border" trigger implanted by flipping signs of otherwise unused weights, pushing the network toward class 0 (and 9) and away from classes 1 and 2 when the border is lit, with no effect on clean data.

**Confidence:** 85%
